gs-earliest-package.title: A package enters the registry
gs-earliest-package.intent: A single gem package card drops into a registry shelf of ordinary packages on 5 May. No avatar or model label.

source.frame: A package artifact enters the registry. No agent avatar, model name or private prompt appears.
lettering: 5 May. September investigators date the earliest package they attribute to this campaign to this day.

gs-earliest-attribution-boundary.title: The artifact and its date only
gs-earliest-attribution-boundary.intent: The same package with its date tag, large; outside the frame edge an empty author slot beyond an evidence limit, labelled later inference.

source.frame: Hold the artifact and its date. Its author remains outside the frame.
lettering: The package is a dated artifact. Identifying its author is a later inference, not something visible to the registry here.

gs-name-identifier.title: A name field highlighted
gs-name-identifier.intent: A package metadata sheet with one field highlighted amber labelled name contains “oai”. The rest of the sheet is untouched; no specimen name.

source.frame: A package-name field is highlighted, with the rest of the artifact unaltered. Do not create a specimen name.
lettering: 8 May. The investigators identify the first package name containing the string oai.

gs-name-limit.title: A clue, not an identification
gs-name-limit.intent: The highlighted name field beside a separate, empty author-identification field.

source.frame: Keep that field distinct from an empty author-identification field in the authored explanatory geometry.
lettering: A name can become an attribution clue. It is not itself a private trace identifying the publisher.

gs-email-gap-web.title: Web publishing requires confirmation
gs-email-gap-web.intent: A maintainer’s change review diagram: the web route passes through a confirmation gate before publishing.

source.frame: A maintainer’s change review distinguishes the web publishing route from the API route.
lettering: The web interface requires account confirmation.

gs-email-gap-api.title: The API route skips the check
gs-email-gap-api.intent: The parallel API route: an unconfirmed account creates a key and publishes, bypassing an empty checkpoint slot.

source.frame: The API path in the reviewed design permits an unconfirmed account to create a key and publish. No actionable request is displayed.
lettering: The change record describes API paths that do not enforce the same requirement.

gs-email-gap-patch.title: The check added
gs-email-gap-patch.intent: Abstract before-and-after code view: two sheets, the right one with a new checkpoint band inserted on the API path.

source.frame: The proposed check is added to the API path in an abstract before-and-after code view.
lettering: The fix closes that gap in the code.

gs-email-gap-merge.title: Merged, not yet deployed
gs-email-gap-merge.intent: A merge record card dated 11 May; a separate production service box beyond a time divider has an empty deployed-date slot.

source.frame: The merge record closes the review sequence. Keep its date visibly separate from the production service.
lettering: GitHub dates the merge to 11 May. That date alone does not establish when production changed.

gs-burst-submissions.title: Over 2,000 submissions
gs-burst-submissions.intent: A dense accumulation of package cards across a two-day span, not in hourly bins; a count strip attributed to the September investigation.

source.frame: Package artifacts accumulate across the two-day interval. Do not distribute them evenly into invented hourly bins.
lettering: The September investigation reports over 2,000 package submissions on 11–12 May.

gs-burst-units.title: Counted units are packages
gs-burst-units.intent: The counted objects are package boxes; behind them three empty slots for agents, compromised developers and thefts, left unfilled.

source.frame: The counted objects stay packages. Leave the identities behind them unpictured.
lettering: This is a count of submissions, not of agents, compromised developers or successful thefts.

gs-email-deployment-deployment.title: The check reaches production
gs-email-deployment-deployment.intent: The confirmation checkpoint moves into the production API boundary; dated 12 May as deployment.

source.frame: The account-confirmation check reaches a schematic production API boundary.
lettering: The investigators date the production change to 12 May.

gs-email-deployment-different-dates.title: Two dates, two questions
gs-email-deployment-different-dates.intent: Two date cards side by side: merge (11 May) and deployment (12 May), each labelled by what it records; no line collapses them.

source.frame: Stay on the changed service, with deployment identified as the kind of event being dated.
lettering: A merge record and a production deployment record answer different questions. The two dates have not been collapsed.

gs-registration-stop-reported-load.title: A status log entry
gs-registration-stop-reported-load.intent: A dated service-status ledger line at 08:54 describes DDoS activity; incoming registration arrows crowd the registration door.

source.frame: A dated service-status record accompanies incoming registration activity.
lettering: 12 May, 08:54 UTC. RubyGems’ status log describes DDoS activity.

gs-registration-stop-registration-disabl.title: Registration closes
gs-registration-stop-registration-disabl.intent: The registration door is now a closed gate; a separate existing-user route beside it is not drawn closed.

source.frame: The new-account registration route closes. Distinguish it from existing users’ package operations.
lettering: Registration is disabled.

gs-registration-stop-consequence.title: Closed to newcomers too
gs-registration-stop-consequence.intent: A generic would-be new account card approaches the closed gate and stops. Not a recovered individual.

source.frame: A would-be new account meets the unavailable registration service. The person and attempted time are not depicted as a recovered individual event.
lettering: The defensive action also closes the service to new registrants.

gs-socket-analysis-analysis.title: Socket publishes an analysis
gs-socket-analysis-analysis.intent: A dated Socket analysis document opens over package artifacts; an aperture examines one package. No person drawn.

source.frame: Joseph Edwards’ dated Socket analysis opens on package artifacts. No personal scene is invented.
lettering: 13 May. Socket publishes its GemStuffer analysis.

gs-socket-analysis-public-material.title: Council material packed into gems
gs-socket-analysis-public-material.intent: Three public council portal buildings (Lambeth, Wandsworth, Southwark) feed page cards into a gem package box.

source.frame: The report’s specimen discussion connects public ModernGov material with packaged copies. Keep narration outside the document rendering.
lettering: Socket describes public material from Lambeth, Wandsworth and Southwark packed into gems.

gs-socket-analysis-contents.title: Classes of public material
gs-socket-analysis-contents.intent: An authored close-up: calendar, agenda listing and committee link cards as separate classes, all clearly public.

source.frame: An authored close-up separates a council calendar, agenda listing and committee link as classes of collected public material. No invented private document is shown.
lettering: The analyzed samples collect calendar pages, agenda listings, committee links and related meeting information from public-facing ModernGov portals.

gs-socket-analysis-follow-links.title: A specimen follows links
gs-socket-analysis-follow-links.intent: Analysis diagram of code behavior: a calendar page link arrow leads to an agenda page, then a second collection round; labelled code analysis, not a log.

source.frame: The report’s specimen diagram follows a calendar link into agenda material. It is explicitly analysis of code behavior, not a logged retrieval with a fabricated timestamp.
lettering: Socket describes a specimen that follows extracted links for another round of collection. Its analysis examines the collection behavior, not just the package names.

gs-socket-analysis-republishing.title: Republished with embedded credentials
gs-socket-analysis-republishing.intent: A package with a sealed embedded credential sends a new package back into the registry.

source.frame: A schematic of the reported package behavior connects embedded credentials with republication. No credentials or executable instructions appear.
lettering: Its analysis describes republication using embedded credentials.

gs-socket-analysis-own-credentials.title: Its own publishing credentials
gs-socket-analysis-own-credentials.intent: An opaque specimen with its own sealed publishing credential inside a self-contained outline; a developer’s machine outside with its keys untouched.

source.frame: A sealed publishing-credential card is included with an opaque specimen. No stolen developer key is inferred from it.
lettering: Some samples carry their own publishing credentials. Socket describes a self-contained publishing environment rather than dependence on credentials already belonging to the machine’s user.

gs-socket-analysis-variants.title: Two paths to the same output
gs-socket-analysis-variants.intent: Two differently shaped publishing routes — via the gem client (terminal) and direct (arrow) — converge on one package-output box.

source.frame: Two differently shaped publishing paths reach the same package-output category. The code, commands and API details are absent.
lettering: Socket finds variants using the package client and variants publishing directly. Different implementation paths lead to the same use of the registry as a public data store.

gs-socket-analysis-archive.title: Data inside a gem
gs-socket-analysis-archive.intent: An archive box open to show collected response sheets inside, visibly different from a library code block beside it.

source.frame: An output archive contains collected response data, visibly distinguished from executable library content. No confidential data is invented.
lettering: In the analyzed specimens, fetched responses are embedded inside valid gem archives. A package-shaped object can hold collected information as well as software.

gs-socket-analysis-counts.title: Two counts in one report
gs-socket-analysis-counts.intent: Two separate count cards from the same report: introduction (>100 gems) and tracker (155 artifacts incl. versions).

source.frame: Two separately labeled narrator’s measures sit beside the source: introduction and tracker.
lettering: The introduction counts more than 100 gems. The tracker paragraph counts 155 package artifacts, including versions.

gs-socket-analysis-downloads.title: Little download activity
gs-socket-analysis-downloads.intent: A download indicator drawn as an almost empty budget bar beside the package cards; no time series.

source.frame: Download activity is shown as a finding of the analysis without inventing a time series.
lettering: Many samples had little or no download activity.

gs-socket-analysis-download-meaning.title: Low downloads, real misuse
gs-socket-analysis-download-meaning.intent: Split: low download bar on the left (few developers reached); publishing-and-storage diagram on the right (registry used as storage). Neither converted into counts.

source.frame: A low download indicator sits beside a separate publishing and storage diagram. Neither is converted into a count of compromised developers.
lettering: Low download activity weakens a picture of mass developer infection, but does not erase misuse of registry publishing and storage. Those are different effects.

gs-socket-analysis-interpretation.title: Purposes open, no attribution
gs-socket-analysis-interpretation.intent: The analysis document with several purpose question cards; an empty attribution slot where a model name would go.

source.frame: The analysis remains open beside the specimens, without an OpenAI model avatar filling its missing attribution.
lettering: Socket considers several possible purposes. Its May report does not attribute the campaign to OpenAI.

gs-cleanup-spam-stopped.title: The spam stops
gs-cleanup-spam-stopped.intent: The status ledger line at 03:17 on 13 May; the incoming arrows are gone, leaving an empty approach.

source.frame: The incoming spam activity stops in the service-status account.
lettering: 13 May, 03:17 UTC. The status log says the spam has stopped.

gs-cleanup-accounts.title: Accounts removed
gs-cleanup-accounts.intent: A row of account cards, several crossed out; no count label.

source.frame: Associated accounts are removed from active use. No account count is invented.
lettering: The response removes accounts.

gs-cleanup-packages.title: More than 500 yanked
gs-cleanup-packages.intent: A grid of package boxes stamped with a yank marker (arrow-up out of the index), still present in an archive tray beneath.

source.frame: More than five hundred package entries are marked yanked, rather than physically erased from all possible archives.
lettering: The update reports more than 500 packages yanked.

gs-cleanup-existing-users.title: Existing users unaffected
gs-cleanup-existing-users.intent: Authored service map: an existing user’s install and push arrows pass freely through the service while the registration gate stays closed.

source.frame: An existing user’s install and push routes remain available in the authored service map.
lettering: The same update says existing users’ installs and pushes were unaffected.

gs-registration-return-restored.title: Registration restored
gs-registration-return-restored.intent: The registration gate opens again at 05:12 on 16 May.

source.frame: The new-account route becomes available again.
lettering: 16 May, 05:12 UTC. Registration is restored.

gs-registration-return-scope.title: Open, not settled
gs-registration-return-scope.intent: The open gate at left; to the right, the earlier packages with question marks for authorship and purpose, untouched by the reopening.

source.frame: Hold the functioning registration boundary rather than a triumphant all-clear for every package or credential.
lettering: This update establishes the return of registration. It does not settle the authorship or purpose of the earlier packages.

gs-later-may-five.title: Five more packages
gs-later-may-five.intent: Five package boxes grouped under a 26–27 May bracket.

source.frame: Five later package artifacts are grouped under the supported two-day interval.
lettering: The investigators identify five further packages on 26–27 May.

gs-later-may-boundary.title: No single hand
gs-later-may-boundary.intent: The five artifacts remain; above each an empty uploader slot rather than one shared hand.

source.frame: The artifacts remain visible without drawing the same hand behind every upload.
lettering: Further artifacts extend the observed activity. They do not identify one continuous run.

gs-june-packages-eighty-three.title: 83 packages on 18 June
gs-june-packages-eighty-three.intent: A dated grid of 83 small package marks.

source.frame: A dated group of package artifacts occupies the registry view.
lettering: The researchers identify 83 packages on 18 June.

gs-june-packages-no-invented-handoff.title: The registry row stays in its row
gs-june-packages-no-invented-handoff.intent: The package group sits inside the registry; at the right edge, a wiki page icon is beyond a hard boundary with a crossed-out arrow.

source.frame: Keep the registry action entirely inside this row. No arrow crosses into a wiki post as if a handoff had been observed.
lettering: The package record gives artifacts and dates. Shared identity and cooperation require additional evidence.

gs-cache-report-report.title: A cache flaw reported
gs-cache-report-report.intent: A sealed vulnerability report card travels to RubyGems on 6 July; the reporter is named only in narration.

source.frame: A vulnerability report reaches RubyGems. The reporter’s name is attributed in narration, with no invented email body.
lettering: 6 July. Luke Marshall reports a cache flaw to RubyGems.

gs-cache-report-exposure.title: Legacy sign-in keys exposed under conditions
gs-cache-report-exposure.intent: Abstract service map: legacy sign-in key path highlighted amber through a cache layer; the package publishing route drawn separately in steel.

source.frame: The legacy sign-in key path is highlighted in an abstract service map, separately from package publishing.
lettering: The maintainer advisory describes conditional exposure of legacy sign-in keys.

gs-cache-report-distinct-system.title: Not the Artifactory flaw
gs-cache-report-distinct-system.intent: RubyGems’ service boundary on the left; OpenAI’s Artifactory route on the right beyond a hard boundary; no connecting line.

source.frame: Keep the RubyGems service boundary clear and do not join it to an Artifactory request route.
lettering: This is a flaw in RubyGems’ cache behavior. It is separate from the Artifactory proxy vulnerability.

gs-cache-fix-root-cause.title: The root-cause fix
gs-cache-fix-root-cause.intent: A service-side patch sheet replaces the faulty cache card, which is crossed out. 9 July.

source.frame: A service-side change removes the faulty cache behavior.
lettering: 9 July. The root-cause fix is deployed.

gs-cache-fix-purge.title: The Fastly cache purged
gs-cache-fix-purge.intent: A separate operation: cached response cards emptied out of a CDN cache box.

source.frame: Cached responses are removed from Fastly as a separate response operation.
lettering: The Fastly cache is purged.

gs-cache-fix-limited-class.title: Only one key class affected
gs-cache-fix-limited-class.intent: Three key classes: legacy sign-in (amber, affected), scoped and short-lived (steel, unaffected with checkmarks).

source.frame: Legacy sign-in keys remain a distinct credential class in the narrator’s diagram.
lettering: The advisory says scoped and short-lived keys were unaffected. The affected class must not be expanded to every RubyGems key.
